title: ConspirED: A Dataset for Cognitive Traits of Conspiracy Theories and Large Language Model Safety
abstract: arXiv:2508.20468v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Conspiracy theories erode public trust in science and institutions while resisting debunking by evolving and absorbing counter-evidence. As AI-generated misinformation becomes increasingly sophisticated, understanding the rhetorical patterns in conspiratorial content is important for developing interventions such as targeted prebunking and assessing AI vulnerabilities. We introduce CONSPIRED (CONSPIR Evaluation Dataset), which captures the cognitive traits of conspiratorial ideation in multi-sentence excerpts (80-120 words) from online conspiracy articles, annotated using the CONSPIR cognitive framework. CONSPIRED is the first dataset of conspiratorial content annotated for general cognitive traits. Using CONSPIRED, we (i) develop computational models that identify conspiratorial traits and the dominant trait in text excerpts, and (ii) evaluate LLM robustness to conspiratorial inputs. translated_title: ConspirED：一个用于研究阴谋论认知特征及大语言模型安全性的数据集
translated_abstract: 摘要：阴谋论侵蚀了公众对科学和机构的信任，同时通过演变和吸收反证来抵抗辟谣。随着人工智能生成的错误信息日益复杂，理解阴谋内容中的修辞模式对于制定干预措施（如针对性预辟谣）和评估人工智能的脆弱性至关重要。我们引入了CONSPIRED（CONSPIR评估数据集），该数据集捕捉了在线阴谋文章中多句摘录（80-120词）的阴谋思维认知特征，并使用CONSPIR认知框架进行标注。CONSPIRED是首个针对一般认知特征进行标注的阴谋内容数据集。利用CONSPIRED，我们（i）开发了识别阴谋特征及文本摘录中主导特征的计算模型，以及（ii）评估了大语言模型对阴谋输入的鲁棒性。我们发现大语言模型容易被阴谋内容误导。
tldr: 本文首次构建了基于认知特征标注的阴谋论数据集CONSPIRED，并利用它开发识别模型和评估大语言模型，揭示了模型易被阴谋内容误导的安全隐患。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CONSPIRED, the first dataset annotated for general cognitive traits of conspiratorial content, and uses it to develop detection models and evaluate LLM robustness, revealing that LLMs are readily misaligned by conspiratorial inputs.
